verdict.rationale: Hands-on community reports say third-party DOM libraries work inside Angular: D3 works in Angular 2 without 'angularizing', and jQuery plugins were easy to integrate in AngularJS. No first-party documentation in the pack describes the DOM-access mechanism. Missing for 10: first-party docs on direct DOM access APIs (e.g. element references, renderer, lifecycle hooks for third-party init/teardown), and evidence for modern Angular versions rather than Angular 2/AngularJS-era reports.

support.subject: As a developer, I can directly manipulate the DOM to integrate existing browser libraries like charting or visualization tools

citations.quote: third-party libs like D3 work without 'angularizing'
